correctness.boundary_check: For x=Q−1, the initial triple (x,−1,−1) yields (P_3,P_2)=(−1,x). Each subsequent triple (x,x,−1) takes (u,v) to (xu,(1+x)u+xv). After j=k−1 such triples followed by the final x, the multiplier is x^j(x+1)(x−1−j)=Q(Q−k−1)(Q−1)^(k−1); the formula also follows directly at j=0. Hence every group of order k+1 admits an additional zero for k≥1 with first character trivial; this does not classify the subthreshold kernel. At q=k+2 the fraction tends to exp(−1). The frozen finite checker was inspected without execution; the algebraic reconstruction is the unrestricted proof.
correctness.rationale: Unnormalized convolution on all of H^n diagonalizes in the character basis. Orthogonality at a supported site gives q−1 or −1, so the multiplier is the path independent-set sum with P_i=P_(i−1)+a_i P_(i−2), P_0=P_(−1)=1. Reducing all activities modulo q gives the 6-periodic sequence 1,0,−1,−1,0,1 starting at i=0. The nonzero residues ±1 exclude zeros off n≡1 mod 3 without requiring q prime. For n=3k+1 use an indeterminate Q in place of q. The constant term vanishes; differentiating in each trivial-coordinate activity at all activities −1 splits the occupied-site weight into segments j−2 and n−j−1. The product is zero unless j≡1 mod 3, where it is (−1)^k, including empty end segments. Thus a zero at q requires q|t for the number t of trivial designated sites. At q≥k+2 this forces t=0. Conversely specified activities −1 at the designated sites propagate P_1=0 to every P_(3h+1), regardless of the two intervening activities. Counting character choices gives nullity q^(2k)(q−1)^(k+1) and the stated rank and fraction (also valid at k=0).

value.rationale: A full kernel characterization for all abelian alphabet structures of a given order determines exactly which Fourier modes are lost. The sharp boundary separates structural zeros from additional arithmetic cancellations and explains a nonvanishing limiting fraction of lost modes at threshold. This is more informative than an isolated determinant evaluation or a recurrence reformulation.
